subject: Flexible commit / credit allocation proposal for Helios Analytics
messages:
From: Samir Desai <samir@helios-analytics.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodai.com>
Date: Fri, 24 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood Hosted API pricing — commit tiers

Thanks Priyom — we reviewed the high-level numbers and have a couple of items we need clarified before we can move to procurement: 

1) If we miss a quarterly commit, do you do an intra-quarter make-good, or is everything reconciled annually? Our finance team prefers quarterly true-ups.
2) How do you treat overage token pricing if we exceed a reserve in a given quarter but stay under the annual commit? Is there a credit applied later?
3) We're interested in a flexible credit pool that can be drawn down by internal teams. Any constraints there?

Can you send the detailed mechanics (worked example with a $/token and credit flow)? Also loop in your finance lead so we can get into procurement rules.

Best,
Samir
Head of Platform Engineering
Helios Analytics

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodai.com>
To: Samir Desai <samir@helios-analytics.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodai.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodai.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodai.com>
Date: Fri, 24 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood Hosted API pricing — commit tiers

Samir — thanks for the quick read. Short answers up front, then a worked example attached.

- Quarterly true-ups: we can do either quarterly or annual true-up. For customers who prefer cadence-aligned billing runs we recommend quarterly true-ups with a 10-business-day settlement window after quarter close.
- Overage handling: overages are billed at the overage rate at time of consumption. If you later remain under your annual committed volume, we apply a make-good credit at the annual true-up to refund difference between overage charges and the effective committed-unit price. That credit posts as a billing credit (not cash).
- Flexible credit pool: supported. We can allocate a prepaid credit bucket tied to the deal that teams draw from. Unused credits either carry to next quarter (if you pick carry-forward) or convert to annual reconciliation credit depending on the selected policy.

I've attached a spreadsheet with two worked examples: 1) quarterly true-up with intra-quarter make-goods, 2) annual true-up with overage-credit reconciliation. See tab "WorkedExamples".

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm preference (quarterly vs annual)
- We finalize commit bands and overage rates in the attached worksheet
- Marissa and I will prepare SOW language for the credit handling and settlement window

 attaching: Commit_Schedule_Q2-Q4.xlsx

Best,
Priyom

From: Samir Desai <samir@helios-analytics.com>

Date: Mon, 27 Apr 2027 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood Hosted API pricing — commit tiers

Thanks Priyom — the spreadsheet helped. A few follow-ups from procurement: 

- Procurement prefers quarterly true-ups but needs the settlement window <= 15 business days. You mentioned 10 business days which should be fine — please confirm that is standard.
- For make-goods: procurement expects credits applied to the invoice following the settlement period, not as a bookkeeping memo. Is that doable?
- We also need language around partial credit carry-forward: if a quarter under-delivers by <5% we allow automatic carry-forward; beyond that we want a credit. Would that be a custom policy or something you support generally?

If you can confirm these three items I can loop in our CFO and get procurement started.

Samir

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodai.com>
To: Samir Desai <samir@helios-analytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodai.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodai.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodai.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Apr 2027 10:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood Hosted API pricing — commit tiers

Samir — answering each: 

1) Settlement window: 10 business days is our standard for quarterly true-ups; we can contract to 15 business days if procurement requires, but that will push the billing credit into the next invoice cycle depending on your billing cadence. We'll reflect either in SOW.

2) Make-goods as invoice credits: yes — we will post make-good as an invoice credit applied to the invoice following the settlement posting. Finance has to sign off but that is standard practice for our enterprise contracts.

3) Partial carry-forward policy: we support a "soft cushion" (configurable) up to 5% for automatic carry-forward. Anything beyond that is treated as shortfall and credited per the make-good rules. This is part of our standard commit policy and can be adjusted in the SOW for enterprise customers.

Marissa — can you confirm finance is OK with invoice credit posting and the 10 -> 15 business day flexibility for this account? Monica — I'll draft the SOW redlines once we get finance confirmation.

On SOW redlines: see "SOW_redlines_20270428.pdf" for proposed language around credits (section 3.2) and carry-forward (section 3.3).

Thanks — Priyom

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodai.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodai.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodai.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodai.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Apr 2027 16:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Flexible commit / credit allocation proposal for Helios Analytics

Priyom — finance confirms: invoice credits are acceptable; we will post the credit on the first invoice after the settlement window closes. We can contractually allow up to 15 business days if the customer needs it — note that pushing beyond 10 days may change cash timing but is fine from an accounting perspective.

I've cc'd Vivek to confirm any risk/ops constraints; Monica, please finalize the SOW redlines and prepare a single-page summary for Samir's CFO. Once Samir confirms carry-forward policy (5% cushion), legal can approve the redline and we route DocuSign.

Marissa

Redwood Inference
